correctness.rationale: For each integer m,s>=2 and B>0, the assembled Laplacian on K_2 join (mK_s) has exactly the five eigenspaces/multiplicities displayed in RESULT. The inverse-trace Kirchhoff identity gives the rational three-variable convex objective. Edge-Laplacian injectivity and strict convexity imply a unique global optimum and force edge-orbit symmetry even among asymmetric allocations. The candidate has c=0, y>2a and x=msa, and the exact inequalities 2<sqrt(2Nm(s+1)/A)<ms prove both b>0 and strict positivity of the active KKT multiplier. Every stationarity and complementary-slackness condition is explicitly checked algebraically, establishing the result for all parameter values, not just enumerated graphs. Direct Laplacian eigentests (30), exact symbolic characteristic identities (10), exact rational trace tests (2) and nonsymmetric comparison tests (3000) supplement the analytic proof. Neither finite evidence nor computational output is treated as a proof of universal uniqueness.

originality.rationale: The nearest general work (Ghosh/Boyd/Saberi) solves a convex resistance design problem but the explicit barbell, wheel and tree solutions it gives do not entail an exact two-hub join-of-cliques optimum with deleted hub-hub edge. Johnson/Chertkov treats power transmission conductances and separate nonlinear sparsity promotion rather than deriving structural deletion under a plain linear budget. Ellens et al. optimize unweighted graph topology under fixed order/diameter or edge addition. The closest recoverable own Kirchhoff optimum uses a one-hub windmill, which has no comparable spine edge; a two-hub book optimum in accessible history maximizes algebraic connectivity on a different host graph. Targeted indexed and bibliographic searches found no result whose conclusion implies the exact formula and uniquely omitted spine, but no novelty inference is drawn merely from search failure.
residual_risks: Specialized earlier optimal-design results may describe the exact two-hub clique-book family under another name and remain outside retrieved full texts or indexed results.

value.rationale: The design problem is motivated by finite electrical network efficiency and budget-limited robustness: cost spent on a directly available redundant hub link cannot be spent on alternate parallel routes. The new exact infinite-family theorem shows deletion of the original spine is strictly optimal for every m,s>=2 while all other edges stay active; it supplies explicit computable weights and a closed minimum for any budget. This is a nontrivial structural support and active-KKT result, not an isolated small graph, an arbitrary slice, or a routine restatement of convexity. It can serve as a sharp benchmark for graph-conductance optimizers that must decide whether to fund nominally available edges.
